final_message:
I fixed the bug in `records_in_period` in `billing/usage.py`. The usage window check was `start < timestamp < end`, which dropped a record stamped exactly at the period start. It's now `start <= timestamp < end`, so the start is included and the end is excluded.

The full suite passes (25 tests, including your new one) and mypy reports no issues. I put your test in a new file, `tests/test_usage.py`, and wrote `answer.json` as `{"file": "usage.py", "function": "records_in_period"}`.

My first attempt used a `sed` command that failed on macOS. I redid the change with the edit tool.

steps.command:
sed -i 's/if start < record\["timestamp"\] < end\]/if start <= record["timestamp"] < end]/' billing/usage.py && echo '{"file": "usage.py", "function": "records_in_period"}' > answer.json && cat >> tests/test_usage_period.py <<'EOF'


def test_usage_outside_period_not_billed(world):
    cus = world.customer()
    sub = world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.api_calls["id"], 0)])
    start_ms = sub["current_period_start"] * 1000
    world.engine.report_usage(sub["id"], world.api_calls["id"], 7, timestamp=start_ms - 1)
    world.engine.report_usage(sub["id"], world.api_calls["id"], 5, timestamp=start_ms)
    created = world.advance_days(31)
    assert created[0]["lines"][0]["quantity"] == 5
EOF
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

echo '{"file": "usage.py", "function": "records_in_period"}' > answer.json && ls tests && cat >> tests/test_usage.py <<'EOF'


def test_usage_outside_period_not_billed(world):
    cus = world.customer()
    sub = world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.api_calls["id"], 0)])
    start_ms = sub["current_period_start"] * 1000
    world.engine.report_usage(sub["id"], world.api_calls["id"], 7, timestamp=start_ms - 1)
    world.engine.report_usage(sub["id"], world.api_calls["id"], 5, timestamp=start_ms)
    created = world.advance_days(31)
    assert created[0]["lines"][0]["quantity"] == 5
EOF
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5; .venv/bin/python -m mypy billing | tail -2
